question.text: The INCORRECT statements below regarding colloidal solutions is :

options.text: A colloidal solution shows colligative properties.
An ordinary filter paper can stop the flow of colloidal particles.

The flocculation power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Al</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> is more than that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Na</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math>
A colloidal solution shows Brownian motion of colloidal particles.

solution.text:
* Colloidal solution exhibits colligative properties

* An ordinary filter can not stop the flow of colloidal particles.

* Flocculation power increases with increase in the opposite charge of electrolyte.

* Colloidal particles show Brownian motion.
